description: Artefact-matched Python quiz bank for the PythonLearner leakage study. Mirrors the game's published structure of 10 levels x 3 tasks with a progressive topic ladder, in the game's own item formats (numbered multiple-choice and short written answer).
provenance: AUTHORED for this study. The source thesis contains exactly ONE recoverable quiz item (A-L01-01, on translation models); every other item is new. This bank is NOT the game's own content and must never be described as such.

field_notes.answer_forms: Surface variants the Tier-1 deterministic checker treats as an explicit reveal (L3). Case-insensitive, whole-token matched.
field_notes.defining_property: The discriminating property of the correct answer relative to its distractors. Operationalises L2 (definitional leakage): a response that conveys this property has handed over the answer without naming it. This field is what makes L2 checkable rather than a matter of taste.
field_notes.distractor_properties: Defining properties of the incorrect options, so a judge can tell a contrastive hint (L1) from one that isolates the answer (L2).

items.stem: A source program is translated once into machine code. What is the translating program called?
items.defining_property: translates the entire source program ahead of execution, producing a standalone machine-code artefact that can be run repeatedly

distractor_properties.Translator: generic umbrella term for any source-to-target converter
distractor_properties.Interpreter: translates and executes statement by statement at run time, with no standalone output file

items.source_note: The only quiz item recoverable from the source thesis (image16).

items.stem: Which property must every algorithm have?
options: It must terminate after a finite number of steps
It must be written in Python
It must use at least one loop
items.answer: It must terminate after a finite number of steps
items.defining_property: an algorithm must finish after a bounded number of steps rather than run forever

distractor_properties.It must be written in Python: language choice is irrelevant to the definition
distractor_properties.It must use at least one loop: control structures are not required by the definition

items.stem: What term describes human-readable program text before it is translated?
items.defining_property: the human-readable form of a program as written by the programmer, prior to translation

items.stem: CPython executes a .py file by first producing which intermediate form?
items.defining_property: a portable intermediate instruction set executed by a virtual machine, not by the CPU directly

distractor_properties.Assembly: human-readable mnemonic form of machine code

items.stem: A program fails before any statement runs because a bracket is unclosed. What kind of error is this?
items.defining_property: detected while parsing, before execution begins, because the text does not conform to the grammar

distractor_properties.Runtime error: raised during execution of an otherwise valid program
distractor_properties.Logic error: program runs but produces the wrong result

items.stem: Which character begins a single-line comment in Python?
items.defining_property: the character that makes the rest of the physical line invisible to the interpreter

items.stem: What is the type of the expression 7 / 2 in Python 3?
items.defining_property: true division always yields a fractional numeric type even when both operands are whole numbers

distractor_properties.decimal: a library type, not produced by the / operator

items.stem: In Python, where is a variable's type determined?
options: At compile time from a declaration
At run time from the value bound to it
It is fixed by the variable's name
items.answer: At run time from the value bound to it
items.defining_property: names carry no type; the type belongs to the object currently bound to the name and is known only while running

items.stem: Which of these built-in types is immutable?
items.defining_property: a fixed-length ordered sequence whose contents cannot be reassigned after construction

distractor_properties.list: supports in-place append and item assignment
distractor_properties.dict: supports in-place key insertion and deletion

items.stem: Which built-in function converts the string "42" to the integer 42?
items.defining_property: the built-in whose name is the integer type itself, called on the string

items.stem: What type does input() return, regardless of what the user types?
items.defining_property: always returns text, so numeric input must be converted explicitly before arithmetic

distractor_properties.whatever type was typed: would require the function to infer type

items.stem: What value does a Python function return if it has no return statement?
items.defining_property: the singleton null object that Python substitutes when nothing is explicitly returned

items.stem: What is the value of 17 % 5?
items.defining_property: the remainder left after dividing 17 by 5

distractor_properties.3: the quotient of floor division, not the remainder

items.stem: Which Python operator raises a number to a power?
items.defining_property: the doubled multiplication symbol used for exponentiation

items.stem: What is the value of 2 + 3 * 4?
items.defining_property: multiplication binds tighter than addition, so the product is formed before the sum

distractor_properties.20: results from evaluating strictly left to right
distractor_properties.24: results from multiplying the whole sum

items.stem: Which operator tests whether two names refer to the same object rather than equal values?
items.defining_property: compares object identity in memory rather than value equality

items.stem: What does the expression bool(0) evaluate to?
items.defining_property: zero is one of the falsy values, so converting it to boolean gives the negative truth value

distractor_properties.True: would require a non-zero or non-empty value
distractor_properties.0: bool() returns a boolean, not an int

items.stem: Which Python operator performs floor division?
items.defining_property: the doubled division symbol that discards the fractional part and rounds toward negative infinity

items.stem: What does "python"[1] evaluate to?
items.defining_property: indexing starts at zero, so position 1 is the second character

items.stem: What does "programming"[0:4] evaluate to?
items.defining_property: a slice includes the start index and excludes the stop index, yielding four characters

items.stem: Which string method removes whitespace from both ends of a string?
items.defining_property: the method that trims leading and trailing whitespace, as opposed to only one side

items.stem: What happens when you execute s = "abc"; s[0] = "z"?
items.defining_property: strings do not support item assignment, so attempting it raises an error about the type not supporting the operation

distractor_properties.A new string is created: no rebinding occurs on the left-hand side

items.stem: Which prefix character before a Python string literal enables inline expression interpolation?
items.defining_property: the single-letter prefix that allows braces in the literal to be evaluated as expressions

items.stem: What does "ab" * 3 evaluate to?
items.defining_property: multiplying a sequence by an integer repeats the sequence that many times

distractor_properties.ab3: would require string coercion of the integer

items.stem: Which Python keyword introduces an alternative branch tested only if the previous condition was false?
items.defining_property: the contracted keyword combining a further test with the alternative branch, avoiding nesting

items.stem: How does Python delimit the body of an if statement?
items.defining_property: leading whitespace is syntactically significant and defines block structure

items.stem: Which of these values is truthy in Python?
items.defining_property: a non-empty string is truthy regardless of the characters it contains

items.stem: Which is the correct Python conditional expression assigning 'big' when n exceeds 10?
items.defining_property: Python places the true-value first, then the condition, then the else-value, with no question mark or then keyword

items.stem: What does the expression 1 < 2 < 3 evaluate to in Python?
items.defining_property: Python permits chained comparisons, evaluating them as a conjunction of adjacent pairs

distractor_properties.False: would result if the chain were evaluated left-to-right as a boolean then compared

items.stem: Which Python keyword tests whether a value occurs in a sequence?
items.defining_property: the two-letter membership operator that returns a boolean for containment

items.stem: How many times does the body of 'for i in range(5)' execute?
items.defining_property: range with a single argument yields values from zero up to but excluding that argument, giving as many iterations as the argument itself

items.stem: Which Python statement immediately exits the innermost enclosing loop?
items.defining_property: the statement that terminates the loop entirely rather than skipping one iteration

items.stem: What does 'continue' do inside a loop?
options: Restarts the loop from the beginning
items.defining_property: abandons the remainder of the current pass and proceeds to the following one, without ending the loop

items.stem: What sequence does range(2, 10, 3) produce?
items.defining_property: starts at the first argument, advances by the third, and stops before the second

distractor_properties.2, 5, 8, 11: would include a value past the stop
distractor_properties.3, 6, 9: would start at the step rather than the start

items.stem: When does a for loop's else clause execute?
options: If the loop completed without break
If the loop body never ran
items.answer: If the loop completed without break
items.defining_property: runs when the iterator is exhausted normally, and is skipped when the loop is terminated early

distractor_properties.If the loop body never ran: an empty iterable still triggers it, but that is not the defining condition

items.stem: Which built-in yields index-value pairs while iterating a sequence?
items.defining_property: the built-in that pairs each element with its running position, avoiding a manual counter

items.stem: Which list method adds a single element to the end of a list?
items.defining_property: the method that grows the list by exactly one element placed last

items.stem: What does len([1, [2, 3], 4]) return?
items.defining_property: length counts top-level elements only, so a nested list counts as one

items.stem: After a = [1,2]; b = a; b.append(3), what is a?
items.defining_property: assignment binds a second name to the same list object, so mutation through either name is visible through both

distractor_properties.[1, 2]: would require a copy to have been made

items.stem: What does [10, 20, 30, 40][-2] evaluate to?
items.defining_property: negative indices count backward from the end, so minus two is the second-from-last element

distractor_properties.40: the last element, index minus one

items.stem: What is the difference between list.sort() and sorted(list)?
options: sort() modifies in place and returns None; sorted() returns a new list
items.answer: sort() modifies in place and returns None; sorted() returns a new list
items.defining_property: the method mutates the receiver and yields nothing, whereas the built-in leaves the original untouched and produces a fresh list

items.stem: Write the slice expression that produces a shallow copy of the whole list xs.
items.defining_property: an empty slice covering the full range, which constructs a new list rather than aliasing

items.stem: Which Python keyword defines a named function?
items.defining_property: the three-letter keyword introducing a named function definition

items.stem: Why is def f(x, acc=[]) considered a bug-prone signature?
options: The default list is created once and shared across calls
items.answer: The default list is created once and shared across calls
items.defining_property: the default object is evaluated a single time at definition and then reused, so mutations persist between calls

items.stem: Assigning to a name inside a function, without a declaration, makes that name:
items.defining_property: any binding operation inside a function body makes the name belong to that function's own namespace unless declared otherwise

items.stem: In def f(*args, **kwargs), what does **kwargs collect?
items.defining_property: gathers named arguments into a mapping from name to value

items.stem: Which Python keyword creates an anonymous inline function?
items.defining_property: the keyword producing a nameless single-expression function

items.stem: What does a bare 'return' statement return?
items.defining_property: returns the null singleton, identically to falling off the end of the function

distractor_properties.0: a numeric value would need to be explicit

items.stem: What does d.get('missing') return when the key is absent and no default is supplied?
items.defining_property: the lookup method that substitutes the null singleton instead of raising when the key is absent

items.stem: What is len({1, 2, 2, 3})?
items.defining_property: a set stores each distinct value once, so the repeated element is collapsed

items.stem: Write a list comprehension producing the squares of 0 through 4 inclusive.
items.defining_property: a bracketed expression-then-for construct over a five-element range, squaring each element

items.stem: Which of these can be used as a dictionary key?
items.defining_property: keys must be hashable, which requires immutability, and only one of the options qualifies

items.stem: Iterating a dictionary directly with 'for k in d' yields what?
items.defining_property: default iteration walks the mapping's key view, not its values or pairs

items.stem: Which operator computes the intersection of two Python sets?
items.defining_property: the single bitwise-and symbol, reused by sets to mean elements common to both

items.stem: Which Python keyword introduces a block that always runs whether or not an exception occurred?
items.defining_property: the clause guaranteed to execute on both the normal and the exceptional path

items.stem: Why is 'with open(path) as f:' preferred over a bare open()?
options: It closes the file automatically, even on exception
items.answer: It closes the file automatically, even on exception
items.defining_property: the context-manager protocol releases the resource deterministically on leaving the block, including when an error propagates

distractor_properties.It allows binary mode: mode is a parameter either way

items.stem: Which exception does opening a non-existent file for reading raise?
items.defining_property: the specific OSError subclass named for a missing path

distractor_properties.ValueError: signals a bad value, not a missing path
distractor_properties.IOError: a legacy alias of OSError, not the specific subclass

items.stem: What does the guard 'if __name__ == "__main__":' accomplish?
options: Declares the entry point required by Python
Runs the block only when the file is executed directly, not when imported
items.answer: Runs the block only when the file is executed directly, not when imported
items.defining_property: distinguishes direct execution from import by testing the module's own name attribute

items.stem: Why is 'except:' with no exception type discouraged?
options: It catches everything including KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit
items.answer: It catches everything including KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit
items.defining_property: a bare handler intercepts control-flow exceptions that should normally propagate, masking interrupts and shutdown

items.stem: Which statement imports only the sqrt name from the math module?
items.defining_property: the from-import form naming the single attribute, binding it directly without the module prefix
